guide.title: How to create an app password in Nextcloud
guide.step1: Open your Nextcloud and click your picture (top right) → Personal settings.
guide.step2: In the left menu, open Security.
guide.step3: Under "Devices & sessions", type a name (e.g. MyHomeLab backups) and click "Create new app password".
guide.step4: Copy the username and password shown and paste them here. The password is only shown once.
guide.generalOrPerService: General or per app: you can use this destination for every backup, or create several (an app password, or even a Nextcloud user, per app) and choose one in each backup.
guide.safety: An app password only gives access to files and can be revoked in Nextcloud at any time without touching your password. MyHomeLab stores it encrypted and only deletes backups it created itself.

backup.description: Saves the Nextcloud calendars, tasks and contacts to a destination, as often as you choose.
backup.included: A .tar with each calendar and task list of the connected account (.ics), each address book (.vcf) and a nextcloud.json with the version, the enabled apps and, with an admin account, the users and groups.
backup.notIncluded: Files, the database and other users’ calendars (except those shared with you) are not included: for the whole machine, back up the VM or CT in Proxmox. Saving into the same Nextcloud protects against accidental deletion, but not against losing the server.
backup.restore: To restore: import the .ics in Calendar (or Tasks) and the .vcf in Contacts.

trek.title: TREK
trek.description: The trip planner: version, security, backups and, through TREK MCP, every trip for the agents (create and change days, places, bookings, packing, budget…).

mcp.secretHint: Stored encrypted in MyHomeLab. The 1-hour token is requested automatically.
mcp.factHint: With the MCP machine client, agents get the whole TREK API, with the scopes chosen there.
mcp.menuOn: On: agents use the whole TREK API.
mcp.menuOff: Off: connect it so agents can work on trips.
mcp.missing: Without the MCP client, agents only see the version and backups.

openGym.title: openGym
openGym.description: The gym and body weight: routines, workouts and the week plan. Jarvis adds plans with catalogue exercises.
openGym.agentsNote: The Personal Trainer uses openGym to see the workouts and add routines. For another agent, pick its tools in Assistant → Workflow.
openGym.notFound: This openGym does not exist or was disconnected.
openGym.accountDescription: The openGym connection, with the pairing token (the same as the phone app). It expires if unused for its lifetime; MyHomeLab saves the renewed one every time it checks.

openGym.tokenHint: openGym renews it halfway through, when MyHomeLab uses it.
